_readme: The multi-host drain campaign, as scenarios. Read with multihost_drain.py --dry-run.
A node designator is an INDEX into --nodes (so this file is cluster-agnostic) or a
hostname. Campaign node order is T(.3)=0, N2(.4)=1, N1(.5)=2, N3(.6)=3; at 4 peers rr
gives one rank per machine, at 8 two, at 12 three.
kind:      clean = no migration, the four-machine oracle for every trial of that shape
seq   = one rank at a time, by signal, the published single-host sequence
cut   = several ranks in ONE batch, by migrate event, under a driver-held lease
ranks:     which ranks migrate (a repeat means the same rank again, at the next epoch)
evacuate:  a node (or list of nodes) whose live ranks all migrate
to:        next | spread | one | <node> | [<node>, ...] positionally per migrating rank
cuts:      single (one cut for all evacuated nodes) | per-node (one cut each, back to back)
place:     rr | block | an explicit {rank: node} map
shape:     one name, or a list meaning 'run this scenario once per shape'
by_shape:  per-shape overrides of any knob, checked before the scenario's own flat value.
The shapes differ ~70x in cost per round cross-host, so a scenario naming a LIST
of shapes cannot be sized with one `rounds`. The defaults block below carries the
measured sizing; a scenario overrides it only where it needs to (B6's 4096-int
payloads).
Phase C scenarios drive the batch path and are refused without --allow-batch until the
C-1..C-3 library fixes land.
_sizing: Rounds are sized from a measured two-point fit of this cluster, 4 ranks one per machine,
ms=1, taken 2026-08-14 against HEAD 571df5f (see runs/mhd1103355 and runs/mhd1104*):
a clean job costs ~0.7 s of fixed overhead plus a per-round cost of, in ms,
and at 8/12 peers the fast shapes cost ~1.55/1.65 ms. Every `rounds` below targets a
~75 s job, which is the window the campaign plan asks for (60-90 s): long enough that a
migration lands well inside the run rather than after it (a SKIP proves nothing), short
enough that the matrix fits its budget. Cross-host is 5.5x single-host on deep_rounds and
1.1x on baseline -- the latency-bound shapes pay the network, the throughput-bound ones
barely notice -- which is why the single-host round counts could not simply be reused.

scenarios.name: B0
scenarios.why: every shape, four machines, nothing migrated: separates 'the cluster is wired right' from 'migration is correct', and its checksums are compared by hand against the single-host table

scenarios.name: B1
scenarios.why: the first cross-host migration: one rank, N2 -> N3, nothing else moving

scenarios.name: B2
scenarios.why: the same rank chained N2 -> N3 -> N1 -> N2 at epochs 0, 1, 2: the trigger's staleness fence and the advertise re-resolution, three machines deep

scenarios.name: B3
scenarios.why: different ranks in sequence: r0 T -> N3, then r2 N1 -> T; the second migration's peers include one that has already moved

scenarios.name: B4
scenarios.why: rank 0, the rank every other rank dials: p2p_ring has no collectives to hide re-establishment behind

scenarios.name: B5
scenarios.why: 8 ranks: N1's two ranks evacuated one at a time onto two DIFFERENT survivors

scenarios.name: B6
scenarios.why: mid-message: variable_payloads with a payload that spans segments, so the drain cuts part way through one, across a machine boundary

scenarios.name: B7
scenarios.why: the remaining migration-relevant shapes: deep recursion, an idle link that must re-establish lazily on a NEW host, and mixed p2p/collective traffic

scenarios.name: B8
scenarios.why: 12 ranks, three per machine: scale, not a new mechanism. Run with --include-optional or --only B8

scenarios.name: C0
scenarios.why: a batch of ONE: isolates the migrate-event path from concurrency, so a failure here is the event plumbing and nothing else

scenarios.name: C1
scenarios.why: evacuate N1, k=2, both onto one survivor: the smallest real batch

scenarios.name: C2
scenarios.why: evacuate N1, k=2, onto two different survivors — a shape the sequenced evacuation never produced

scenarios.name: C3
scenarios.why: 12 ranks, k=3 in one cut, spread over the three survivors

scenarios.name: C4
scenarios.why: TWO machines emptied in ONE cut, k=4, onto the other two: the thesis' R2.2 at full width

scenarios.name: C5
scenarios.why: k=2 mid-message: the batch counter cross-check is the byte-exactness oracle here

scenarios.name: C6
scenarios.why: explicit placement puts ranks 2 and 3 — ring NEIGHBOURS — on one machine, so the two migrators seal against each other across hosts (rr never produces this: it places r and r+4 together)

scenarios.name: C7
scenarios.why: two cuts back to back (N1, then N3): the lease race guard between them — the second SET NX must not race the first batch's release

scenarios.name: C8
scenarios.why: negative: while a cut is in flight a second batch must be refused the lease, and the job must still finish with the baseline checksums
